name: House of Nobles
summary: In Stormwind Keep, the House of Nobles holds the kingdom’s lands, taxes, and trade. Their refusal to pay the laborers who rebuilt the city set off bloody riots that shook the realm.

sections.title: Aristocrats of the Realm
sections.body: Stormwind’s greatest patrician families form the House of Nobles, the Crown’s chief council. They own most arable land in Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, and so hold great sway over trade, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. Boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rule Stormwind in name. Yet the council can bind the throne in red tape, stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial affairs.

sections.title: Bureaucratic Paralysis
sections.body:
With King Varian missing, the nobles leave outlying territories to fend for themselves, yet wield royal authority in petty disputes. Darkshire’s officials seethe after the House overturned their death sentence for grave robber Dextren Ward.

The nobles ordered him spared and sent to the Stormwind Stockade instead. The execution of Blackrock Orc chieftain Targorr the Dread has also been delayed indefinitely. A scheming noble would use him as a political pawn, while local sentries watch Stormwind rot from within.

sections.title: Whispers of Treason
sections.body: The House of Nobles’ stubbornness reaches beyond greed. Lady Katrana Prestor, secretly the black dragon Onyxia, has manipulated the council and paralyzed the kingdom. During talks with the stonemasons, she fed the aristocracy’s arrogance and urged them to hoard royal funds. Lord Gregor Lescovar and other high-ranking nobles conspire with the Defias Brotherhood in the throne’s shadow. No imperial troops march to aid the outlying towns.

sections.title: The Labor Revolt
sections.body:
After the Second War, the House of Nobles hired Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild Stormwind City from its ashes. At the same time, the nobles ran up great debts while pushing the kingdom’s military frontier south into Stranglethorn. Once the gleaming capital was finished, they balked at the bill and withheld the workers’ full wages.

Betrayed, the masons rioted in the streets. The nobles banished the guild, driving the ruined workers into Westfall, where they formed the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: What is the House of Nobles?
aliases: what is the house of nobles
who are the nobles in stormwind
faq.answer: The House of Nobles is Stormwind’s ruling assembly of aristocratic families, whose titles and seats pass through inheritance. Its members advise the monarch and control much of the kingdom’s domestic policy, taxes, and labor laws.

faq.q: Why did the House of Nobles refuse to pay the Stonemasons?
faq.answer: Stormwind’s nobles overextended the treasury with costly military expeditions southward into Elwynn and Stranglethorn. When Edwin VanCleef presented the bill for rebuilding Stormwind City, they could not pay. They offered only a fraction of the promised sum, then ordered the guild disbanded.

faq.q: What happened when the Stonemasons rioted?
faq.answer: When the House of Nobles refused payment, the stonemasons rioted in Stormwind’s streets. The nobles banished the guild, and the ruined workers fled to Westfall, where they became the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: Why won't Stormwind send troops to help Westfall or Duskwood?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles controls the realm’s purse strings and administrative approvals. Its members repeatedly block funding, troop deployments, and municipal aid to outlying territories, leaving local forces such as the People’s Militia and the Night Watch isolated.

faq.q: Who was Lord Baurles K. Wishock?
faq.answer: Lord Baurles K. Wishock is an influential noble pressing for an investigation of the warlocks beneath The Slaughtered Lamb. The consequences of his inquiry unfold in the warlock storyline.

faq.q: Did all the nobles turn against the Stonemasons?
faq.answer: No. Count S. J. Erlgadin supported the masons and fought to improve their wages and working conditions. Disgusted by his peers’ betrayal, he gave up his title and seat, left society, and joined Hemet Nesingwary’s expedition in Stranglethorn.

angles.text: For humans of Westfall and Duskwood, the House of Nobles means arrogant highborn in a marble palace, while common folk bleed defending their homesteads from bandits and monsters.
The nobles’ bitter quarrels, corrupt dealings, and dirty secrets offer work for fixers, cutpurses, and master cheesemonger Elling Trias.
Influential nobles are turning their attention to Stormwind’s practitioners of the dark arts beneath The Slaughtered Lamb.
The House of Nobles holds power in Stormwind City’s court but little sway over the wider Grand Alliance. Its stinginess keeps threatening the southern human territories’ stability.
